page.h1: HTS Chapter 73: Articles of Iron or Steel — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Steel Articles by Market (HTS Ch. 73) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Mexico, Canada, the EU, China, the UK, Japan, Brazil and Korea charge on U.S. fasteners, pipe, fittings and other steel articles, with Canada's 50% surtax and EU and UK steel quotas.
keywords: canada tariff on us steel products

intro: Four of the eight largest markets charge nothing on most U.S. steel articles: Mexico and South Korea under free-trade agreements, the EU since July 1, 2026, and Japan on its own low schedule. The exception is **Canada**, the second-largest buyer: it charges a 50% surtax on nearly every steel line of the chapter, CUSMA or not. **China** adds 10% to its 3–8% rates, and Brazil's Mercosur tariff runs 14–18%. For pipe and tube the tariff column is not the whole story: the EU and the UK cap duty-free imports with steel quotas and charge 50% above them, and EU importers must report and pay for embedded carbon under CBAM.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Canada is the second-largest market ($5.81B, down 13.2%) and the one where tariffs bite hardest. Since September 8, 2026 nearly every steel line of the chapter, including fasteners (7318, $1.27B), structures (7308) and fittings (7307), pays a 50% surtax even when it qualifies for CUSMA. Canada remits the surtax for some listed products it finds in short supply or not made in Canada, mainly seamless tube, rails and sheet piling, and, until June 30, 2027, for steel used to make vehicles and aircraft.

assumptions: Each cell uses one representative six-digit subheading per heading: the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports (for example 7318.15 for fasteners, 7326.90 for other articles, 7306.30 for welded pipe). MFN rates are World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple averages for 2023, the latest year WITS holds; national 8–10-digit lines can differ.

Mexico (USMCA), Canada (CUSMA) and South Korea (KORUS) apply 0% only to goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; the normal-rate column shows the MFN rate a non-qualifying U.S. good would pay. Mexico's MFN figures include its decree of December 29, 2025 (in force January 1, 2026) where it raised a line under the representative subheading.

Canada's cells add the surtaxes on goods of U.S. origin named in the Canada Gazette: the United States Surtax Order (Steel and Aluminum 2025), SOR/2025-95 as amended by SOR/2026-187 (Schedule 2.1 at 50%, Schedule 2 at 25%), and the United States Surtax Order (2026), SOR/2026-186. Products remitted under Schedules 2 and 6 of the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025) can enter without the surtax; they are not netted out.

For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes chapter 73 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029; the normal-rate column shows the EU rate before that date. The 50% above-quota duty of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 is shown for the headings TARIC lists under it (7301.10, 7302.10, 7302.40, 7304, 7305, 7306).

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to the MFN rate. China's 2019 counter-tariffs (5–25% by annex, for example 10% on the 47 Chapter 73 lines in Annex 3 of Announcement 2019 No. 3) are not added, because importers can hold line-by-line exclusions valid until December 31, 2026.

Canada's other steel surtaxes do not stack on U.S. goods: its global 25% Steel Derivative Goods Surtax (SOR/2025-267, since December 26, 2025, on fasteners, wire, chain, structures and similar goods) excludes goods already under the U.S. steel surtax, and its steel tariff-rate quotas apply only to countries outside CUSMA.

The UK cells show the UK Global Tariff and, for rails and welded pipe and tube, the Steel Trade Measure quotas from July 1, 2026 (50% above quota). Anti-dumping duties, VAT and the EU's CBAM charge are not included.
